title: The board people have carved for 2,000 years: a short history of Nine Men's Morris (4-minute video)
text:
Three squares, one inside the other, twenty-four points. People have carved this pattern for at least two thousand years: an Egyptian temple roof (with a disputed date), Roman steps, the Gokstad Viking ship, the cloister benches of English cathedrals, a muddy village green in Shakespeare. We made a short video about where the name comes from, the rules, a Chinese cousin called fangqi, why a game a computer solved in 1996 is still worth playing, and the game we built from it, Millfall.

Watch: https://youtu.be/07tmcBw4GQ4

Chapters: 00:00 Twenty-four points · 00:24 Where the name comes from · 00:42 Kurna, Egypt · 01:09 Rome: Ovid · 01:33 The Gokstad ship · 01:44 The Middle Ages · 02:09 Shakespeare · 02:26 Fangqi · 02:42 The rules · 03:16 1996, a solved game · 03:45 Millfall

Historical scenes are AI-generated pixel art (PixelLab); narration is synthetic (Kokoro); gameplay is from Millfall. Main source: Wikipedia, Nine men's morris.

title: Ascended — the Moonbeam execution at the Star Shrine (one of 33)
text:
Close a mill and your piece walks over and executes the enemy. This one is the Star Shrine's Moonbeam: the beam takes the victim straight up. One of 33 executions across 4 arenas, recorded in-engine, no cuts.
